events.title: The "Day of Two Noons" Creates Standard Time Zones
events.description: American and Canadian railroads put four standard continental time zones into use. Thousands of conflicting local times were replaced by one system. In many cities, clocks were reset at midday, which is how the day got its nickname.
events.significance: Standard time brought order to railway scheduling and later became the basis for the time zones used around the world.

events.title: Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty Signed
events.description: U.S. Secretary of State John Hay and Philippe Bunau-Varilla signed a treaty giving the United States rights to build and control a canal across Panama. The signing came about two weeks after Panama declared independence from Colombia.
events.significance: The treaty made the Panama Canal possible. It also shaped U.S.–Panama relations for most of the 20th century.

events.title: Mickey Mouse Debuts in Steamboat Willie
events.description: Walt Disney's short cartoon Steamboat Willie premiered at the Colony Theatre in New York City. It was one of the first cartoons to use synchronized sound, and it introduced Mickey Mouse to a wide audience.
events.significance: The film launched one of the world's most recognizable characters and helped build the Disney entertainment empire.

events.title: Jonestown Tragedy in Guyana
events.description: More than 900 members of the People's Temple died in Jonestown, Guyana. Most of them drank a cyanide-laced beverage on the orders of cult leader Jim Jones.
events.significance: It was one of the largest losses of American civilian life in a deliberate act before September 11, 2001. It remains a lasting warning about the dangers of extreme cult control.
